questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Ishika saw the tiger in the forest.

options.text: The tiger saw by Ishika in the forest.
The tiger was seen by the forest in Ishika.
The tiger was seen by Ishika in the forest.
The tiger sees Ishika in the forest.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active voice sentence becomes** the subject.**
 
• The verb **"saw"** in active voice is changed to **"was seen" **in passive voice.
 
• The subject of the active voice sentence** "Ishika"** becomes the agent in the passive voice sentence, introduced by the preposition **"by".**
 
• The location **"in the forest"** remains unchanged and is placed at the end of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The tiger was seen by Ishika in the forest."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The tiger saw by Ishika in the forest." – Incorrect structure; the verb form "saw" does not fit in passive voice.
 
• **Option 2:** "The tiger was seen by the forest in Ishika." – Incorrect order and context; "in Ishika" is incorrect placement.
 
• **Option 4:** "The tiger sees Ishika in the forest." – This is in active voice, not passive.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

She has been __studying for two o'clock__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence **requires** a correct expression of time to indicate when the studying began.
 
• The present perfect continuous tense **(has been studying) **is used to show an action that started in the past and is still continuing.
 
• **"Since"** is used to indicate the point in time when the action started.

Therefore, the correct phrase is "**studying since two o'clock**".

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She has been studying **since**__ two o'clock."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "study from two o'clock"** – Incorrect, because "study from" implies a different time frame not associated with 'has been studying'. 
 
• **Option 3: "study for two o'clock"** – Incorrect, as it suggests studying in preparation for something happening at two o'clock, which is not the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4: "studying two o'clock"** – Incorrect, as it is grammatically incorrect and lacks the proper preposition to indicate time.
